text:
Jesper Bratt has 22 points in 23 games, and 18 of them are assists, which tells you the shot isn't falling. He has four goals on 6.2 expected (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and the Devils as a whole have finished below their chances with him on the ice. That is a finishing slump, not a decline. New Jersey takes 62% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, eight points better than without him, one of the best marks on the team.

This is the player Evolving-Hockey's model loved last season: 98th percentile among forwards for driving play against tough competition, with more expected wins than actual ones. Our range has him around 72 points, and his rate per 60 minutes is running above it. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows 72% of his exits leaving the zone with possession. He was a sixth-round pick in 2016 and is closing in on another franchise legend on the Devils' lists, per Heavy.com. If the goals arrive, they arrive in bunches.
